issues.failure_explanation: The proof establishes density convergence \(\phi_\sigma^c\to\phi_\sigma^0\), but the field estimate concerns the reconstructed computable field \(u_\sigma^c\), not the exact Neumann PML solution \(u_\sigma\). The cited estimate \eqref{eq:pde-conv} only compares \(u\) with \(u_\sigma\). No argument is supplied to bound \(u_\sigma^c-u_\sigma\) (or \(u_\sigma^c-u_\sigma^{\rm ni}\)) in terms of the density error and the exponentially small kernel difference. Hence the field convergence is unsupported as written.

failure_location.quote: The compact-field estimate follows directly from the exact PML-PDE convergence estimate \eqref{eq:pde-conv}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a comparison between the computable reconstructed field and the exact Neumann PML solution (or nearest-image corrected field), splitting the reconstruction formulas and using the density convergence plus the exponential decay of the kernel difference in the physical region to bound the difference.
issues.overall_effect: The density convergence and unique solvability parts of Theorem thm:computable-convergence remain established. The field convergence guarantee for the computable PML-BIE and the final exponential error bound for the physical solution are not rigorously proven.
issues.title: Unsupported field convergence in computable PML-BIE theorem
issues.why_classification: The defect is a missing but contained comparison argument. The main density convergence is already proven, and existing kernel estimates likely suffice to repair the field estimate without new global architecture or loss of the advertised rate.
